text.en: The children build a tool to measure turns, using tracing paper and a straw fixed at the centre of a circle.

The book makes an angle measuring tool from tracing paper or thin board with a straw fixed at the centre. Mark the starting point on it.
Show an eighth turn of the straw. An eighth turn is half of a quarter turn. Then show two eighths (a quarter), three eighths, and so on up to eight eighths, which is a full turn.
To measure an angle, place the centre of the tool at the point of the angle, line up one arm with the start mark and read the turn made by the other arm. You may need to add measures, such as a quarter plus an eighth.
Guess first and then check: is the angle acute, right or obtuse, and how many eighth turns is it?
You can also draw angles for given turns using the straw as a guide, for example 3 eighth turns.
(additional, not in the textbook) Later we measure angles in degrees. A full turn is 360 degrees, a half turn 180, a quarter turn 90 and an eighth turn 45 degrees.

problem.en: An arrow turns a quarter and an eighth. How much turn is that?

text.en: The total is 3/8 of a turn.

why.en: It is more than a quarter and less than a half, so obtuse.

prompt.en: How will you measure an angle using the turn tool?

requiredIdeas.en: Put the centre on the point and align one arm
Read how many eighth turns the other arm makes
Say if it is acute, right or obtuse

commonMisconceptions.en: Starting the measure from the wrong line

points.en: Eighth turns let us measure smaller angles.
Eight eighth turns make a full turn.
In degrees, a quarter turn is 90 and a full turn is 360 (additional).
